biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Prevotella and Klebsiella, reduced bacteria associated with healthy status and overgrowth of bacteria such as Prevotella and Klebsiella
biomarker_name.notes: Multiple biomarkers identified across metagenomic and metabolomic analyses representing dysbiotic microbiota and altered metabolites in hypertension.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: SBP, DBP, MBP measured by tail-cuff method. Shannon index based on genera profile.
biomarker_unit.notes: Units vary by biomarker type: relative abundance for bacterial genera, mmHg for blood pressure, index for diversity measures.

value: 26 metabolites altered in both pHTN and HTN
biomarker_value.evidence_quote: 48.21% pHTN, and 45.45% HTN are found in enterotype 1. 44 genera were differentially enriched. AUC of up to 0.91 and 0.89
biomarker_value.notes: Values reported for enterotype distribution, differential abundance, and classification performance. Specific abundance values for individual genera and metabolites are in supplementary tables.

disease_response_os.notes: This is a microbiota dysbiosis study in hypertension, not an oncology trial. Overall survival is not applicable to this study design.

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable; study does not track survival outcomes.

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status is not reported. This study focuses on microbiota dysbiosis in hypertension, not cancer or advanced disease progression.

value: Reduced Faecalibacterium, Oscillibacter, Roseburia, Bifidobacterium, Coprococcus, Butyrivibrio
Decreased amino acid biosynthesis and transport
feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: dramatically decreased microbial richness and diversity, Prevotella-dominated gut enterotype, distinct metagenomic composition with reduced bacteria
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal microbiota phenotypes described through metagenomic and taxonomic profiling in hypertension and pre-hypertension populations.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; this is a microbiota dysbiosis in hypertension study, not an oncology study.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; no tumor measurements in this cardiovascular/microbiota study.

value: Cohort: 41 healthy controls, 56 pre-hypertensive subjects, 99 primary hypertension patients
Study population: Chinese employees of Kailuan Group Corporation, Tangshan
Sample type: Fecal metagenomic DNA sequencing (Illumina platform, 1211 Gb total)
Metabolomic analysis: LC/MS on serum (n=124; 30 controls, 31 pHTN, 63 HTN)
Animal model: Germ-free C57BL/6L mice transplanted with human microbiota
Blood pressure measurement: Tail-cuff method in mice; mercury sphygmomanometer in humans
Exclusion criteria: Cancer, heart failure, renal failure, smoking, stroke, peripheral artery disease, chronic inflammatory disease, antibiotic/probiotic use within 8 weeks
Gene catalogue: Non-redundant genes (95% sequence identity threshold, CD-HIT)
Sequencing depth: 6.18 ± 1.43 million reads per sample (average)
Statistical method: Wilcoxon rank sum test, Kruskal-Wallis test, random forest classification
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: cohort of 41 healthy controls, 56 subjects with pre-hypertension, 99 individuals with primary hypertension; 1211 Gb 125-bp paired-end reads
uncurated_metadata.notes: Study design, participant characteristics, analytical methods, and technical specifications relevant to microbiota dysbiosis investigation in hypertension.

host_species.evidence_quote: 196 Chinese individuals; Male GF mice aged 8–10 weeks were randomly distributed into two groups
host_species.notes: Primary study conducted in human subjects (Chinese population); validation and mechanistic studies performed in germ-free mice (Mus musculus C57BL/6L strain).

extraction_warnings: Paper is aggregated population-level study with 196 participants across 3 groups. Individual sample-level data (subject_id, sample_id, individual age, individual sex) cannot be extracted without access to supplementary tables or raw data.
For sample-level extraction, only group-level metadata can be reliably reported: 41 controls, 56 pre-hypertensive, 99 hypertensive participants total.
Sequencing platform inferred as 'IlluminaHiSeq' from technical specs; exact model not explicitly named in Methods.
NCBI accessions mentioned as available online but not provided in paper text.
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 1 subgroups ['healthy controls', 'pre-hypertension', 'hypertension', 'HTN mice (recipient after procedure)', 'control mice (recipient after procedure)'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.
Paper is a microbiota study in hypertension, not a cancer/tumor study; many schema fields (disease_response_orr, RECIST staging, TNM staging) are not applicable
Age data for human participants not reported in accessible sections; only stated for mice recipients (8-10 weeks)
BMI values referenced as analyzed but not explicitly stated in results
FMT donors described as 'two patients of HTN and one normotensive control' but study-specific identifiers not provided
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
ECOG performance status and tumor size measurements are not applicable to this microbiota dysbiosis study and are reported as 'not_reported'.
Overall survival data is not collected in this study; participants were not followed for mortality outcomes.
Disease response metrics (RECIST, CR/PR/SD/PD) are not applicable; this is not an oncology trial.

Biomarker values are primarily reported as statistical comparisons (P-values, fold-change) and classification metrics (AUC) rather than absolute quantitative values; see supplementary tables for individual abundance data.

The study includes both human metagenomic/metabolomic data and experimental animal data (fecal transplantation in mice); granularity is study-level for human cohort, with separate animal experimental results.
